name: A10-0034/2026 – Mariateresa Vivaldini, Kristian Vigenin – Provisional agreement – Am 15
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directives 2014/65/EU and (EU) 2022/2557 as regards the extension of certain mitigating measures available for small and medium sized enterprises to small mid-cap enterprises and further simplifying measures
part_text: AMENDMENTS BY THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT\* to the Commission proposal DIRECTIVE *(EU) 2026/…* OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of … amending Directives 2014/65/EU and (EU) 2022/2557 as regards the extension of certain mitigating measures available for small and medium-sized enterprises to small mid-cap enterprises *with a view to simplification (Text with EEA relevance) THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 53(1) and Article 114 thereof, Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission, After transmission of the draft legislative act to the national parliaments, Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee, After consulting the Committee of the Regions, ▌ Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, Whereas: (1) ‘Europe's Choice: Political Guidelines for the next European Commission 2024-2029’ sets out a plan for the Union’s sustainable prosperity and competitiveness. Making business easier and deepening the internal market are among the plan’s key priorities. (2) The Commission’s communication of 29 April 2021 entitled ‘Better regulation: Joining forces to make better laws’ also supports the competitiveness of Union enterprises by aiming to ensure that Union legal acts achieve their objectives, at a minimum cost. In its communication of 16 March 2023 entitled ‘Long-term competitiveness of the EU: looking beyond 2030’ and its communication of 29 January 2025 entitled ‘A Competitiveness Compass for the EU’, the Commission identified the need to rationalise and simplify reporting requirements for enterprises and administrations and committed to reducing the administrative burden by at least 25% for all enterprises and at least 35% for small and medium-sized enterprises (‘SMEs’). (3) On 12 September 2023, the Commission published a communication entitled ‘SME Relief Package’, announcing its goal to help SMEs compete and grow by being attentive to the needs of enterprises that, due to their growth, exceed the thresholds set out in the definition of SMEs, and the broader range of small mid-cap enterprises (‘SMCs’). Action 18 of that communication provided that the Commission would develop a harmonised definition for SMCs, build a dataset based on that definition, and assess possible measures to support SMCs in their growth, including the potential application, in adapted form,
